proposal.summary: Preserve one demonstrated evidence-reuse procedure. The empty-output finding is inconclusive at this snapshot, and both stalled-search signals reflect required searches over an already known entity set.

edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across mixed search and fetch workflows
edits.content: When a task requires both single and batched research operations, keep a URL-keyed cache of fetched text. Select URLs directly from structured search hits, validate official-source requirements using parsed hostnames, deduplicate batch URLs, and exclude URLs already successfully cached. Reuse cached text when building the evidence supplied to a grouped, schema-validated extraction call. Validate extracted citations against the same cached text and verify exact requested entity coverage before recording constraints. Exercise extra tool modes only when the task requires them; an empty new-entity discovery record can be appropriate when a search supplies evidence for already known entities.

additional_candidates.description: URL deduplication and cache reuse supported mixed single/batched research and a grouped extraction with successful local validation.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, but this snapshot ends after constraint logging. The root code invokes refinement before assigning answer content and readiness, and no completed final worker iteration is visible. Five extracted rows passed local validation, and all twenty constraint calls returned true. This supports a timing limitation, not a demonstrated submission failure or recovery; a failure memory would overstate the evidence.

Both flagged batch queries returned four hits and recorded no new entities after the single search had already recorded the complete requested set. The task explicitly required batched searching. The first query supplied table sources used in fetching and extraction; the second supplied overlapping sources and an appendix with limited usefulness. Neither occurrence demonstrates an uncontrolled search loop, and no search was repeated after extraction.

The search code filters parsed official hostnames; the fetch code deduplicates batch URLs, excludes the singly fetched URL, and reuses its cached text. Execution confirms four fetched pages and cache reuse, followed by five schema-validated rows with no local validation failures. Preserve this bounded procedure without claiming final submission success. No existing entries are available to update.

proposal.summary: Update discovery tracking to recognize aliases and strengthen the existing recovery skill with semantic completeness checks. Retain the covered fetch-recovery procedure.

edits.title: Inspect search results and reconcile aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, handle each query in input order. Reconcile names against known entities before deciding they are new: punctuation variants, omitted initials, and contextually unambiguous surnames can refer to already discovered people. Maintain an evidence-backed alias mapping; do not merge ambiguous names automatically. Exact string inequality alone does not establish a new entity. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier empty event. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including verification searches that supply useful missing-field evidence; do not invent discoveries to suppress a stall warning.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered pages
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific unresolved fields before fetching again. Audit populated cells too: nonempty values and matching quotations do not establish complete meaning, correct entity attribution, or the required time. Track excerpts, summaries, and ambiguous attributions as unresolved when the task requires fuller evidence. Review saved evidence first to distinguish extraction omissions from retrieval gaps. Apply shared statements to each explicitly covered entity, while preserving distinct statements for subgroups. Request concise factual summaries and brief supporting excerpts for the remaining gaps; when exact wording is required, seek the complete relevant statement rather than substituting a summary or adding editorial notes to the value. Test a revised focus on one page before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus so later responses do not overwrite earlier evidence. Keep unstated fields unresolved and use alternative sources rather than inferring them from birthplace or institutional location. Validate quotations against an individual saved response, then check semantic support, scope, entity, and time before committing repairs. Matching rendered text does not authenticate it as a direct quotation from the underlying page. FETCH_FAILED calls for bounded retries and source switching instead.

additional_candidates.description: Exact-string novelty checks recorded name variants and surnames as newly discovered entities.
Evidence audits and targeted repairs recovered incomplete populated fields that passed quotation membership and missing-cell checks.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern already discovered people: six year-level nationality searches, three targeted affiliation/nationality searches, four individual nationality searches, and three final audit searches. Their empty discovery records are consistent with verification, and subsequent fetches supplied useful evidence. The existing memory explicitly permits honest empty verification results. These signals do not demonstrate consistently bad memory outcomes; the separate alias-recording defect warrants the update below.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel URLs, then LIGO, EurekAlert, Campus France, Scientific American, Le Monde, Tokyo, Nature, two nationality sources, and two later Nature pages. The run tracked attempted URLs, tested a small alternate-source batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through usable alternative evidence, including a CV and a professional-society announcement. Clean URLs and a PDF also failed, so malformed suffixes remain an unsupported causal explanation. Entry 1 already covers bounded retries, source switching, and evidence-based recovery; its usage and outcomes do not justify deletion or another overlapping edit.

The discoveries list labels omitted-initial variants, alternate apostrophes, and later bare surnames as new entities after their full names were already recorded. The trajectory's exact-string known_names comparison explains this reusable bookkeeping failure. Final row uniqueness recovered output coverage but did not correct discovery history. Extend the existing discovery memory instead of creating another entry.

The trajectory reported no quotation failures while retaining a summarized motivation, an incomplete motivation excerpt, and weak entity attribution. Later audits found these defects; even a subsequent 'Missing cells: []' coexisted with an explicitly incomplete value. Targeted evidence retrieval and repairs resolved the gaps before final validation. This repeatable successful audit-and-repair tactic extends the existing incomplete-page skill, whose empty usage/outcome lists provide no basis for declaring it ineffective. Preserve the distinction between rendered-text membership and underlying-page quotation authenticity.

proposal.summary: Update two existing memories to prevent alias-based discovery inflation and audit criteria drift. Fetch failures are already covered by the revised availability memory.

edits.title: Inspect discoveries and reconcile entity aliases
edits.content: After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, do this separately for each query in input order. Do not emit empty placeholders before inspection or assume later records erase them. Compare entity identities rather than exact name strings: reconcile punctuation, apostrophe, initials and shortened-name variants against the existing roster using contextual evidence. Keep aliases internally; do not count a known person's alternate spelling as a new discovery. Do not merge ambiguous identities without evidence. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including useful verification searches. A stalled_search signal alone does not establish lack of research progress; assess whether the search supplied evidence for unresolved fields.

edits.title: Separate quotation support from audit criteria
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, labels and assembled passages. Verify the entity, requested time period and every substantive component before recording a positive constraint verdict. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested field: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without establishing legal citizenship; citizenship requires explicit citizenship evidence. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Treat reviewer findings as hypotheses to resolve against saved evidence and the task contract, not as new requirements. Do not reject a source excerpt solely because the fetch tool renders text, or add an organizational parent as a separate affiliation without evidence that the requested scope requires it. For composite claims, retain a mapping from each component to its source excerpt and never stitch passages into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

additional_candidates.description: Exact-string roster comparisons counted alternate spellings of known people as new discoveries.
Reviews substituted citizenship for nationality and sometimes treated rendered excerpts or organizational parent names as automatic defects.
Saved retrieval versions, focused patches and semantic reviews recovered missing or unsupported cells.

decisions.reason: All 29 occurrences were considered: four fallback searches returned known entities, nine nationality searches verified the roster, eleven gap searches sought missing evidence, and five final targeted searches addressed remaining cells. Their empty discovery records were appropriate rather than premature placeholders. Several supplied useful evidence despite finding no new people. The existing memory already permits honest empty records; repeated signals across its outcomes do not establish that this guidance is harmful.

All 26 occurrences were considered: nine initial same-host failures, six failures in the next mixed batch, seven during nationality retrieval, two gap-source failures and two final targeted failures. The nationality batch retried previously failed LIGO and AP URLs; an APS URL also failed after an earlier successful retrieval. Alternative-host probes and subsequent sources enabled recovery. Entry 1 was already revised during this run to require probes, preserve evidence and track failed URLs. Its usage records concern version 1, so these outcomes do not demonstrate that the current version 2 is consistently bad. No additional host blacklist or causal claim is justified.

The discoveries log records shortened names and an apostrophe variant as new after their corresponding people were already discovered. The trajectory's fallback comparison uses exact string membership. This is distinct from legitimate empty verification records and supports adding identity reconciliation to the existing discovery memory.

The second audit explicitly required citizenship although the requested column was nationality, producing additional objections; later prompts restored the distinction. Reviews also rejected some plain rendered excerpts and demanded an organizational parent before a focused resolution retained the existing affiliation. These recovered process failures warrant clarifying the existing semantic-support memory. Passing citation membership checks do not resolve these interpretation questions.

The trajectory preserved page_versions, checked quotes against individual retrievals, repaired targeted cells and validated the final structure and coverage. These successful tactics substantiate retaining entries 2 and 3, whose outcomes show no deterministic issues. A separate skill would substantially duplicate existing guidance; the two edits prioritize concrete gaps instead. The passing self-check confirms mechanical recovery, not independent factual completeness.
